text:
mira: Quick sync — proposing final attribute lexicon for LLM spans. trying to keep ops + privacy tradeoffs small. list below, pls react

kai: 👍 can you paste the exact names? need to validate against exporters and grafana dashboards

mira: sure — rough proposal (feel free to bikeshed):
```
redwood.llm.model.name = string (e.g. "redwood-1")
redwood.llm.model.variant = string (quantization/arch tag)
redwood.llm.model.revision = string (semver/gitsha)
redwood.llm.request.routing = string (route id: hosted|dedicated:region)
redwood.llm.request.input_tokens = int
redwood.llm.request.output_tokens = int
redwood.llm.request.tokens_bucket = string (low/medium/high or 0-50/51-200)
redwood.llm.cache.hit = bool
redwood.llm.cache.type = string (kv_prefix/prefix_kv)
redwood.llm.latency.ms = double
redwood.llm.error = string (optional)
```

james: overall looks good. couple notes:
- prefer to keep raw token counts as attributes for debug traces, but we should also emit aggregated token metrics in the pipeline to avoid searching spans for metrics
- for exporters: add a processor that strips or buckets tokens if export config retention < 30d

kai: agree with james. also: cardinality is a concern for `model.revision` and `routing` — recommend we only include `revision` when trace-level debug flag is set, otherwise send `model.variant` only

zoe: privacy check: do not include any prompt text or user identifiers in spans. token counts are fine, but do not send hashed prompt or embeddings. also think about `cache.hit` semantics leaking workload shape? might be ok but document it

mira: good call. we'll never put prompt or input text in spans. for cache semantics, we'll add `redwood.llm.cache.hit` (true/false) and `redwood.llm.cache.reason` only for internal telemetry (not exported by default)

kai: one more: for low-cardinality dashboards, prefer `tokens_bucket` + percentile histograms on `llm.latency.ms`. exact counts go to metrics as `counter.redwood.llm.tokens` emitted by the collector

james: +1. Implementation plan:
- span attribute naming finalized -> runtime emits both attrs + a metrics envelope for tokens/requests
- pipeline processors: bucket tokens, drop sensitive attrs, sample high-volume model variants at 0.1 if retention short
- exporters: by default, traces -> long-term store (90d), span-attr-heavy fields excluded from external exports unless allowlist

mira: rough rollout timeline: PR by EOD, small canary to observability stack next week, full rollout after 2 days of canary metrics look good

devops-bot: deploy triggered by mira/observability: llm-span-attr-lexicon v1 -> canary (obs cluster) :rocket:

kai: will add dashboard panels for `redwood.llm.request.tokens_bucket` + `cache.hit` rate and `latency P50/P95`

zoe: also add a short note in the privacy doc about attributes we never export: `prompt.*`, `user.*`, full prompt hashes. thank you

mira: thanks team — i'll open the PR with the final attribute list and link to the canary playbook. if no objections in 24h i'll merge

james: minor: document the naming prefix `redwood.llm.` in the OpenTelemetry semantic conventions doc so integrations pick it up

mira: done — will include example span snippet in the PR and a tiny collector pipeline config for bucketing

kai: :thumbsup:
